figure_discussions.caption: Inflow Performance Relationship (IPR) Curves. Analytical linear-PI and Vogel inflow relationships.
figure_discussions.title: Inflow Performance Relationship (IPR) Curves
figure_discussions.observation: PI Model (linear): bottomhole flowing pressure, pwf spans 0–300 bara across the plotted cases. Vogel Model (two-phase): bottomhole flowing pressure, pwf spans 0–300 bara across the plotted cases.
figure_discussions.mechanism: An IPR relates liquid or gas deliverability to drawdown; curvature reflects the selected inflow law and reservoir phase behavior.
figure_discussions.implication: A high zero-backpressure intercept does not establish a producible operating rate because tubing and facility backpressure still have to be satisfied.
figure_discussions.recommendation: Calibrate the appropriate inflow law against well tests and intersect it with a verified tubing relationship on the same rate and pressure basis.

figure_discussions.caption: Gas-Oil Ratio vs Depletion Pressure at Reservoir Temperature.
figure_discussions.title: Gas-Oil Ratio vs Depletion Pressure at Reservoir Temperature
figure_discussions.observation: Molar GOR spans 6.001–62.51 gas moles / oil moles across the plotted cases. Gaps retain undefined phase quantities or hydraulic states that fail the stated operating boundary; they are not interpolated.
figure_discussions.mechanism: As pressure falls, dissolved light components evolve into a gas phase and change the gas and liquid volumes.
figure_discussions.implication: Gas-handling demand can increase relative to oil rate during depletion; a static initial GOR can therefore understate future bottlenecks.
figure_discussions.recommendation: Distinguish fixed-composition flashes from depletion with gas withdrawal, and couple the appropriate PVT path to separator and compression capacity.

figure_discussions.caption: Fluid Density and Temperature vs Depth. NeqSim properties evaluated along prescribed temperature and pressure gradients.
figure_discussions.title: Fluid Density and Temperature vs Depth
figure_discussions.observation: Across the assumed 0–3000 m depth interval, density spans 159.4–323.9 kg/m³ and temperature spans 50.0–140.0 °C.
figure_discussions.mechanism: Depth changes both hydrostatic pressure and temperature; these effects jointly alter fluid density.
figure_discussions.implication: A constant-density hydrostatic approximation can bias bottom-hole pressure, particularly for compressible or near-saturation fluids.
figure_discussions.recommendation: Integrate density over the pressure–temperature path and compare with measured gradients before using the profile for well control or inflow calibration.
figure_discussions.editorial_review: Plot-specific interpretation reviewed against executed source and numerical data.

figure_discussions.caption: Relative Permeability Curves (Corey Model). Analytical Corey relative-permeability model.
figure_discussions.title: Relative Permeability Curves (Corey Model)
figure_discussions.observation: $k_{rw}$ (n_w=3.0): relative permeability, kr spans 0–0.4 across the plotted cases. $k_{ro}$ (n_o=2.5): relative permeability, kr spans 0–1 across the plotted cases.
figure_discussions.mechanism: The Corey curves allocate effective flow capacity between phases according to saturation, residual saturation and fitted exponents.
figure_discussions.implication: Their endpoints and curvature can control water breakthrough and mobility predictions; the plotted curves are constitutive assumptions rather than EOS results.
figure_discussions.recommendation: Replace the illustrative parameters with rock-type-specific core data and examine hysteresis and endpoint uncertainty in reservoir forecasts.
